messages.author: e76ee7aca2448522
messages.subject: INLA infinite loop?
parts:
Hello,

I'm trying to implement LatticeKrig in INLA as an rgeneric model, but I'm running into an issue where INLA seems to run forever. If there were an error message, it would probably be easier to fix, but since there isn't I'm not sure what's going wrong. The last message that INLA gives before freezing up is:

"Called from: eval(expr, p)"

and comes after loading the required packages and libraries into the rgeneric model. I checked the dimension of the A and Q matrices, and their largest dimension is only 1228 in the full stack. Also, there are only 2 hyperparameters as currently implemented. Interestingly, the INLA process doesn't appear to be using my computer's CPU, but is using at most 200 megabytes of memory. Also, the amount of memory used decreases with the runtime. I've attached part of the code leading up to the INLA call, along with the output after the call to INLA. Any idea what could be going wrong? Any help would be much appreciated.

Thanks!

-Johnny

P.S. This is only part of the code, but I can always send more if necessary.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA infinite loop?
parts:
Thx for your email. If there is an error in the rgeneric it can be hard to track, as things can go arbitrary bad.

  You can ‘browser()’ in the rgeneric code to enter the debugger while running.

Not sure if you can do this from within R or it has to be done from the terminal.

There is also an debug option in rgeneric.define which you can turn on to see if you find something.

 

Let me know…

H

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] INLA infinite loop?
parts:
In the first version of my own rgeneric code, I had a million "print" statements for debugging. (And I tried with 20x20 matrices first)

You can also try using inla.rgeneric.q() for some debugging.

PS: The rgeneric functionality is so flexible and "user-defined" that I'm not sure it is reasonable to expect others to check your code for you.

Haakon

messages.author: e76ee7aca2448522
messages.subject: Re: INLA infinite loop?
parts:
Ah, I realized it was a really silly mistake on my end: I was calling an older version of the rgeneric model without realizing it.  I definitely did not realize the browser() function could be called from within an INLA call in terminal, though, or about the debug option in rgeneric.define.  Those will very good to know for the future.  Also, I wasn't able to find the inla.rgeneric.q function.  Is it for producing the Q matrices, because what I had been doing was calling the rgeneric class with cmd="Q" and the initialized hyperparameters.

Thanks again,
Johnny

messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Re: INLA infinite loop?
parts:
Good its solver. Yes, the browser() works within the code and you can even load compiled C-code, f.ex, from your rgeneric model. If you install the testing version, you’ll have access to the ….q function, for which you can test the output of your function.
